sample_unit: classifications (from 100 patient feedback samples); benchmark of 49,140 classifications from 1,170 feedbacks

links.outcome: Logical hallucination rate in LLM feedback classification with vs without SLCA (self-consistency across repeated runs)
links.effect: SLCA reduced logical hallucinations among detected categories from 15.80% (168/1063) to 0.51% (4/786) with GPT-4 and from 7.17% (51/711) to 1.67% (10/599) with Llama-3.1.
links.quote: SLCA reduced logical hallucinations among detected categories from 15.80% (168/1063) to 0.51% (4/786) with GPT-4 and from 7.17% (51/711) to 1.67% (10/599) with Llama-3.1, with residual errors confined to the emergency feedback category.

links.outcome: Residual errors in emergency feedback category after SLCA
links.effect: Residual logical hallucinations after SLCA were confined to the emergency feedback category.
links.quote: SLCA reduced logical hallucinations among detected categories from 15.80% (168/1063) to 0.51% (4/786) with GPT-4 and from 7.17% (51/711) to 1.67% (10/599) with Llama-3.1, with residual errors confined to the emergency feedback category.

unlisted_practices: Self-consistency plus logical-consistency validation (chain-of-thought enforcement) to reduce LLM logical hallucinations in text classification

screen.reason: Evaluates a self-logical consistency assessment guardrail/verification framework applied to LLMs to mitigate logical hallucinations in classifying patient feedback.
